teams.heading: Jake White eyes trusted Springbok ally as Fiji assistant, no name confirmed
teams.body: Jake White's search for a South African assistant to join his Fiji staff is still open. SA Rugby Magazine reported in mid-October that the head coach was turning to a trusted Bok ally, and recent reports say he is eyeing a Springbok ally for the coaching team. No official announcement of an assistant has appeared, and no name has been confirmed. Fiji meet France in Lyon on Saturday.

lead.why: No new Fiji event broke today, so this returns to the open assistant-coach search, the only live Fiji thread in the pack.

teams.heading: Charlie Atkinson says England are aiming for World Cup gold medal
teams.body: England A fly-half Charlie Atkinson, a Gloucester back with one cap, starts against Argentina in Bath on Friday evening, and he says the squad is chasing the title. "The feeling is that we're aiming for the gold medal," Atkinson says. "There's no reason not to aim for that trophy." That ambition sits against a Six Nations in which England lost four games for the first time in 50 years. England's World Cup pool is Tonga, Zimbabwe and Wales.

lead.why: It is a new, quote-driven England story that is not the Curry injury already covered, and it rests on named players and a concrete ambition.

teams.heading: France lead north as Springboks head to Paris, AP reports
teams.body: AP's preview has France as the favourite to reach the Nations Championship final at Twickenham on 29 November, though Scotland, England and Ireland sit alongside them on 2-1 records. The Springboks and New Zealand are the only unbeaten sides, and South Africa lead on points difference. The Springboks visit Paris next week, and AP recalls they beat France there a year ago with 14 men.

lead.why: It is the only new France item not already covered by today's team-announcement editions, and it sets France's place in the Twickenham final race against the Springboks.

teams.heading: Dan Sheehan dismisses Irish decline talk as 'nonsense' ahead of Argentina
teams.body: Sheehan has "full confidence" in the group and wants Ireland to "fully back ourselves" before the Argentina game at the Aviva Stadium. The 28-year-old Leinster hooker is captaining again with Caelan Doris injured, and Ireland sit third in the world rankings despite a string of double-digit losses to South Africa, New Zealand and France. He conceded improvement is needed "across a lot of areas", with set-piece the priority: "Obviously, set-piece is something we need to continue to drive."

lead.why: A captain's direct response to outside talk of decline, with two outlets covering it and concrete supporting facts, is the freshest Ireland story on the shortlist.

teams.heading: Quesada says Italy must try to be unpredictable against Rassie Erasmus' Springboks
teams.body: Ahead of Saturday's Nations Championship match at the Allianz Stadium, Gonzalo Quesada wants Italy to keep the Springboks guessing. At the team announcement he also called Rassie Erasmus the best coach in the world, a compliment from the Italy boss to his South African counterpart before a Test against the reigning world champions. Italy are without a long list of injured players, including captain Michele Lamaro.

lead.why: Quesada's own words on how Italy plan to play South Africa are a fresh item that the previous editions have not covered.

teams.heading: Townsend recalls Huw Jones from injury, picks Kyle Rowe at fullback
teams.body: Townsend's side for Saturday's clash with New Zealand was named on Thursday, and it is a near-total overhaul: only Gregor Brown and Rory Sutherland survive from the starting XV that beat Fiji in July. Huw Jones comes back from injury to partner captain Sione Tuipulotu in midfield, while Kyle Rowe gets the nod at fullback ahead of Blair Kinghorn. Matt Fagerson returns from a groin problem at blindside, and Darcy Graham and Duhan van der Merwe, Scotland's top two try scorers, miss out on the matchday squad.

lead.why: It is the freshest new item about Scotland's own selections, and the other new items are about New Zealand or are opinion pieces.

teams.heading: Louie Hennessey named among Wales replacements for Japan, chasing first home cap
teams.body: Bath centre Louie Hennessey has been named among Wales's replacements for Saturday's Nations Championship match against Japan, and with it the chance of a first Test cap on home soil. He made his Test debut in Dublin earlier this year. Steve Tandy spoke of "lots of competition for position within the squad", and a bench berth for a player still to earn a home cap fits that picture.

lead.why: The full Wales team announcement is a fresh event, and Hennessey's bench place is a new angle the centre-pairing story I already covered does not offer.

teams.heading: Santiago Carreras and Thomas Gallo ruled out of Pumas' Ireland test
teams.body: Full-back Santiago Carreras and prop Thomas Gallo are both out of Friday's Nations Championship meeting with Ireland, unavailable through injury as Felipe Contepomi reshapes the side that drew 28-28 with Australia in September. Number 8 Pablo Matera is one of the few who keep a place from that Test, and Contepomi's stated goal for the three Tests is to be a more polished unit.

teams.heading: Kurtley Beale recalled to Wallabies squad at 37 for England Test
teams.body: Kurtley Beale, 37, is back in the Wallabies squad for Sunday's Test against England at Twickenham. "I just kept believing, I felt like there was some unfinished business," he said. He was last recalled at 35, then ruptured an Achilles playing club rugby, an injury that can end careers. Les Kiss has backed him to compete for a World Cup place, and Beale is closing on a first Wallabies Test in five years.

teams.heading: Eddie Jones challenges Japan to create history by beating Wales in Cardiff
teams.body: Japan have never won at the Principality Stadium, and Eddie Jones wants Saturday's Nations Championship match to end that. He calls the ground "one of the most iconic rugby stadiums in the world" and says his side have a chance to get right at kick-off. The margin was tight: Japan lost there 24-23 in November 2025, beaten by a last-gasp Jarrod Evans penalty. Jones also expects a noisy Cardiff despite the thousands of empty seats forecast, saying the crowd will still be a Welsh cauldron.

lead.why: It is the freshest Japan-focused item not already covered, and it gives Jones's view on the stakes of the Cardiff match.

teams.heading: Jeff Wilson says only 'bizarre officiating' can stop All Blacks against Scotland
teams.body: Wilson, speaking to Sport Nation, is 'pretty confident' the All Blacks can finish the season strong and go through November unbeaten. New Zealand have never lost to Scotland, but they needed a late rally for a 25-17 win in Edinburgh in 2025, and Wilson admits they have made hard work of many recent Tests. Of the things the All Blacks cannot control, officiating is the one he could spot that might prevent victory at Murrayfield on Saturday.

lead.why: A named pundit's verdict on the Scotland test, tied to the Saturday fixture and backed by concrete record facts, is more useful to a fan than the Rennie tackle-law story already reported.

teams.heading: Springbok Malcolm Marx signs long-term Bulls deal, returning home from July 2027
teams.body: The Bulls announced on Thursday that Malcolm Marx will return to South Africa with the Pretoria side from July 2027 on a long-term deal the club has not detailed. The 32-year-old hooker, a two-time World Cup winner with 94 Springbok caps, is the 2025 World Rugby Player of the Year and leaves Japanese side Kubota Spears. His arrival follows that of flanker Kwagga Smith, who also moves from Japan, having signed a three-year contract with the Bulls.

lead.why: It is the freshest South Africa event in the pack, a Springbok hooker's move back to the Bulls, and none of the other new items are about the Springboks' own squad.
